newsitem.title: MEXICO: Cemex Q2 operating profit forecast up.
newsitem.headline: Cemex Q2 operating profit forecast up.

text.p: Cement giant Cemex will likely post higher revenues and operating profits in the second quarter but a lower net return because of Mexican accounting methods, analysts said.

A survey of seven analysts by Reuters found average forecasts of per share net earnings of 0.885 pesos in the second quarter compared to 1.36 pesos, adjusted for inflation, in the second quarter of last year.
Analysts said the expected decline in net profits is because of reduced monetary gains. Monetary gains are declining due to lower inflation in Mexico.
Second quarter revenues are estimated at an average of 7.065 billion pesos, compared with an adjusted figure of 5.854 billion pesos in the second quarter of 1996.
Operating profit is seen at 1.684 billion pesos, compared to 1.438 billion pesos in the second quarter a year earlier.
"Second quarter could post the results we have been waiting for, with the company firing on all cylinders," said Bear Stearns in a report released on Thursday.
But it added that the company would be hard-pressed to maintain the first quarter's low interest expenses.
Analysts said the company's second quarter Spanish operations should reinforce the upward trend in volume growth seen in the first quarter.
"We forecast volume growth of 5.0 percent year-over-year to roughly 1.62 million tonnes, the highest level since second quarter 1995," Bear Stearns said.
Results from other subsidiaries should also help the company's consolidated results.

"The consolidated margins could be better, helped by Vencemos -- the Venezuelan unit of Cemex -- which had very strong prices, and the Colombian unit, which could also help the results," said Carlos Perezalonso, with ABN Amro.
